ai.description: The Mhadei caecilian reaches 20–25 cm. It is dark grey to purple-brown with a pale snout and vent. Distinctive features include 115–125 primary annuli and a lack of secondary grooves.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis mhadeiensis* is distinguished from similar Indian caecilians by its unique combination of a higher number of primary annuli (120–128) and a distinctively rounded snout.
ai.habitat: The Mhadei caecilian inhabits moist, shaded soil within tropical evergreen forests and plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 100 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mhadei caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small soil invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis mhadeiensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 10–18 eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females exhibiting parental care.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis mhadeiensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Goa, India, where it occurs at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Mhadei Caecilian emits a low-pitched, pulsed "tick-tick" sound, typically heard from within damp soil or leaf litter in its humid forest habitat.
